newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMP unit bids 25c/shr for Equatorial.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMP unit bids 25c/shr for Equatorial.

text.p: Quay Mining Pty Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society, offered 25 cents cash for all the shares it does not already hold in Equatorial Mining NL, the AMP said.
The AMP issued a formal Part A takeover document on Monday, it said.
The AMP said it currently owns 99.3 million shares in Equatorial Mining or about 31 percent of its issued capital.
The offer price represents a premium of 22 percent over the closing market price of Friday and a significant premium over the average price throughout 1996, it said.
There is no minimum acceptance condition.
The offer values Climax at about A$79 million.

"We are confident in the strategy being pursued by the board and management of Equatorial Mining, a strategy which we realise may take some time to come to fruition," said deputy managing director of AMP Investments and Quay Mining chairman, Leigh Hall.

"In making this Part A offer, AMP is expressing its willingness to increase the holding that we manage in Equatorial Mining so that the company's plans can be fully implemented," he said in a statement.
"The on-going development of the company will require further equity injections, to fund projects requiring supplementary project financing," Hall said.
"There will also be a need to fund future working capital requirements until the company can generate sufficient operating profit and resultant cash flows," he said.
Equatorial Mining is involved in the development of the El Tesoro copper project in Chile which is expected to be in production in late 1998, the AMP said.

Equatorial Mining also recently announced it has acquired the option to purchase the Mineral Park copper mine in Arizona and the Tonopah copper ore body in Nevada, from Cyprus Climax Metals Co, the AMP said.
It is expected that Equatorial Mining will fully develop these properties as soon as possible, subject to due diligence and the preparation of a bankable feasibility study for the Tonopah property.
Equatorial said it will make an announcement once it has had the opportunity to consider AMP's offer.
